text: The source defines pure stabilizer states as the Clifford orbit of the computational reference state.

For finite n-qubit systems with matched Pauli-phase conventions, the unique common +1 eigenstates of rank-n stabilizer groups are exactly the semantic Clifford orbit of the computational reference state.

logical_form.conclusion: psi is a rank-n stabilizer common eigenstate iff psi is in the semantic Clifford orbit of the computational reference state

text: The full stabilizer free-state set STAB is the convex hull of pure stabilizer states, with ordinary nonnegative probabilities summing to one.
A state preparable within the stabilizer subtheory is free; a state outside that free set is a magic resource state.

A stabilizer protocol is built from Clifford unitaries, adjoining stabilizer ancillas, computational-basis measurement, discarding subsystems, and conditioning these operations on measurement outcomes or classical randomness.

A magic monotone is a family of real-valued state functions that does not increase on average under any stabilizer protocol: if outcome i occurs with probability p_i and output sigma_i, then sum_i p_i M(sigma_i) is at most M(rho). An individual postselected branch may increase.
For finite n-qubit systems, STAB_n is the convex hull of all pure n-qubit stabilizer states; rho is nonstabilizer (magic in the free-set sense) exactly when rho is outside STAB_n.

logical_form.conclusion: rho is free iff rho in conv(pure stabilizer states); otherwise rho is nonstabilizer
